messages:
olivia: Heads up — after the key rotation earlier today several staging pods started returning 403s when calling S3. Noticed the app error shows 'AccessDenied: Invalid token'. Anyone seen this pattern with SA/secret reprojections?
samir: Hmm, did the projected service-account token TTL change or did we swap the IRSA role?
olivia: We rotated a KMS key and re-encrypted the secrets in sops -> git. Then applied helm which updated the k8s Secret. No manual IRSA changes.
mike: Do the pods mount the secret directly or use projected tokens from the ServiceAccount?
lee: They mount a secret named myapp-credentials in the ns staging-123 (helm release: myapp-staging). The deployment refs it via envFrom: secretRef.
kate: Could be a shadowing issue: chart creates a secret + we also have a sync controller that writes a different secret name. If the SA is still bound to old projected creds, the app might be reading an older mount.
olivia: Example of our values (short):
```yaml
secrets:
  secretName: myapp-credentials
  create: true
```
and deployment snippet:
```yaml
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ .Values.secrets.secretName }}
```
samir: Also confirm the ServiceAccount annotation hasn't been lost: on EKS we need eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn on the sa for IRSA. If a reconcile replaced the SA without the annotation pods might get a different token.
mike: Can you paste the SA manifest from the namespace?
olivia: quick paste:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: myapp-sa
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/myapp-staging-role
```
infraction: infra-bot: rotation-webhook: observed Secret/myapp-credentials update in staging-123 at 1975312400. Triggered rolling annotation on Deployment/myapp (no restart).
lee: infra-bot note makes me think we only updated the Secret contents, not the pods. If the app reads secret at start and caches creds in-memory, they won't pickup new secret until restart. But your error was an S3 token error, which suggests the token used to request S3 was invalid server-side.
kate: Another angle — if the controller that syncs secrets from the tenant store creates an immutable secret (immutable: true) then updating gets a new secret name and helm might still point to old name. Check for two secrets: myapp-credentials and myapp-credentials-v2.
olivia: I just checked: there are two secrets. Helm updated myapp-credentials to new value, but sync-controller created myapp-credentials-tenant which the deployment wasn't referencing. Ugh.
mike: Fix options: (1) update deployment to point to the correct secret name (quick), (2) trigger a rollout restart of pods, (3) align sync-controller to overwrite the same secret name.
lee: For short-term, rollout restart is fastest: kubectl -n staging-123 rollout restart deployment/myapp. That forces pods to read new secret.
olivia: Doing that now. Thanks.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollout restarted deployment/myapp in staging-123 by olivia at 1975312545 :rocket:
mike: After restart, watch logs for token refresh and S3 calls. If still 403, we need to check STS/assume-role logs for the IRSA flow.
olivia: Pods are back up, calls look green. No more 403s. Will follow up with a Helm + sync-controller change to avoid name drift.
lee: For followup PR, consider: (a) make secretName deterministic and owned by one system, (b) emit warning in sync-controller when it creates a new secret name, (c) add a k8s preflight that checks for duplicate secrets in a ns.
katE: tiny nit — also set automountServiceAccountToken: true/false explicitly on SA to avoid surprises.
olivia: Good call. I'll open an infra PR with notes and link the rollout change. Thanks all :thumbsup:
